messages:
kevin: Customer on mobile app reports partial SSE responses and frequent reconnects over last 2 days. They see a lot of short 200s then connection closes. Logs: `write -> EAGAIN` and occasional `EPIPE`.

sara: Thanks — can you paste the customer request flow + SDK version? Also any correlation id?

kevin: app v3.4.1, RN-based, uses our streaming SDK with default chunking. correlation: cid=app-8421. Repro steps below.

kevin: Repro (on linux):
```bash
# simple SSE consumer that reproduces the hang
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=rw-large&route=prod"
```
When network is flaky (simulate with `tc qdisc netem loss 10% delay 200ms`), stream gets partial JSON events then `connection reset` after a few seconds.

maria: Do we see any associated 429s or auth refresh noise? Also check whether reconnects are being billed as new sessions.

kevin: Customer says token refresh happens on reconnect, so yes new connections each time. Billing spike reported.

eng-matt: This looks like classic slow-consumer backpressure: the server keeps writing frames into socket send buffer, client can't drain due to poor network or event loop stall, kernel returns EAGAIN then our write path retries eventually hitting abort path. Two quick reproduction asks: 1) can you get a pcap around the disconnect, 2) server side `strace` on write syscalls to confirm EAGAIN patterns?

kevin: I grabbed a short strace from a replica during an incident window:
```
write(46, "data: {\"choices\": [\n", 24) = -1 EAGAIN (Resource temporarily unavailable)
write(46, "data: ...", 512) = -1 EAGAIN (Resource temporarily unavailable)
write(46, "\n\n", 2) = -1 EAGAIN (Resource temporarily unavailable)
close(46) = -1 EPIPE (Broken pipe)
```

sre-jen: Good capture. Two infra things to check immediately: 1) proxy/nginx/haproxy buffering and proxy_write_timeout; 2) any TCP rate limiting or conntrack timeouts on their NAT. If proxy buffers entire response then our runtime sees backpressure differently.

eng-matt: On the runtime side we should try to reproduce with a client that simulates slow reads (sleep in read handler). Also try smaller write chunk sizes (e.g., 512 -> 256 bytes) and lowering cross-request batching to see if that reduces EAGAIN frequency. Quick idea: adaptively reduce chunk size when we see repeated EAGAIN vs maintaining single large write.

maria: For the customer: recommend short-term mitigations: enable client-side exponential backoff (increase reconnect delay), set keepalive pings in the app to avoid stuck half-open sockets, and avoid token refresh on reconnect by using session tokens where possible. We'll also review billing -- forward to finance if they were charged per-reconnect. :money_with_wings:

support-bot: Uploaded logs to /support/attachments/1987654321/cid-app-8421.tar.gz

kevin: Also found nginx proxy on customer's infra doing `proxy_buffering on; proxy_buffers 4 8k;`. If their proxy is buffering responses, a slow client could cause their upstream to stall and then close.

eng-matt: Suggestions / action items:
- engineering: add metric for consecutive EAGAIN per-stream + backpressure event counter.
- runtime: implement adaptive chunk throttling (experiment: batch->chunk size reduction on first 3 EAGAINs).
- devex: add sample code snippet for clients to handle slow consumers gracefully.
- infra/sre: check proxy timeouts and increase `proxy_send_timeout` where safe.

sre-jen: Also consider kernel-level knobs for send buffer size (`/proc/sys/net/core/wmem_default`) on dedicated hosts, but be cautious — bigger buffers can hide slow clients and increase memory pressure.

kevin: From customer side they will try switching to our websocket fallback (less buffering on some proxies) and test with increased client read frequency. Tracking next steps with cust support case 9241.

maria: Can eng attach a short patch that logs EAGAIN counts per connection (non-viz) so we can validate the hypothesis in prod? If yes, we can toggle via feature flag.

eng-matt: I'll push a small instrumentation PR behind a flag today, will ping when deployed.

deploy-bot: Deployed feature-flag scaffolding to staging (ff/backpressure-logs).

kevin: Thanks — I'll update the customer and ask them to test the websocket fallback and increased backoff. Will report results here. :thumbsup:
